title: Annotate genomic intervals by overlap with genes, repeats, or variants

sources.locator: Overview; Usage and option summary; -wo/-c/-v/-f/-r; -split; -sorted
bedtools intersect examples: alignments/genes, exons/repeatMasker, SV/segmentalDups, and multiple databases
Intersecting CpG islands and exons; overlap bp, counts, non-overlaps, reciprocal thresholds, sorted files, multi-file intersections

scientific_use: Compare genomic feature sets to identify overlapping, non-overlapping, or sufficiently overlapping pairs; report overlap base pairs, counts, original records, or annotate one query against multiple feature databases. The tutorial demonstrates CpG islands against exons and other annotation/feature sets.
tool_role_basis: The sources describe applying the existing bedtools intersect command to BED/GFF/VCF/BAM inputs; the scientific work is interval comparison, not implementation of the overlap algorithm.
inputs: A query feature file and one or more B feature files in supported BED/GFF/VCF or BAM forms; examples use reads, genes/exons, repeats, structural variants, segmental duplications, CpG islands, GWAS SNPs, and ChromHMM annotations.
For sorted-mode processing, both inputs must be position grouped/sorted; genome-order file may be required to validate a custom chromosome order.
Spliced BAM or blocked BED12 features require an explicit decision about whole-span versus block-wise overlap.
outputs: Overlapping pairs, overlap base-pair counts, per-query hit counts, query records with any/no hits, or multi-database annotations according to requested reporting mode.
dependencies: bedtools 2 command line; no repository-specific setup established by the inspected examples.
BED/GFF/VCF/BAM parsing conventions and compatible chromosome naming/order; optional upstream sorting for -sorted.
evidence: The intersect page defines pairwise feature overlap, supported formats, overlap fractions, strand filters, counts, reporting forms, sorted algorithm, and split-feature semantics.
The example-usage page grounds the operation in reads-versus-genes, exon-versus-repeat and structural-variant-versus-segmental-duplication questions.
The tutorial demonstrates CpG island/exon overlap outputs and states that examples use separate files such as cpg.bed and exons.bed.
limitations: The named tutorial inputs cpg.bed, exons.bed, and other files are not identified here by accession, immutable source, or provenance; do not treat their names as dataset records.
The result depends on coordinate conventions, genome assembly, feature granularity, strand and overlap thresholds; these must be fixed by a task author.

title: Measure feature depth and breadth over defined intervals

sources.locator: Overview; Usage and option summary; Default behavior; -hist and -d
bedtools coverage examples: aligned reads over 10-kb windows and BEDGRAPH-derived summaries

scientific_use: For each interval in A, quantify how many B features overlap and what fraction of A bases are covered by at least one B feature; can assess breadth and depth for genomic windows or target regions and emit per-base or histogram summaries.
tool_role_basis: The documentation describes using bedtools coverage on existing interval or alignment data. No new coverage algorithm is implemented by the example workflow.
inputs: A set of target intervals (example: genome-tiling 10-kb windows) and B sequence-alignment/feature intervals in BED/GFF/VCF/BAM-compatible forms.
Coverage direction is A measured by B; the page notes this interface changed at version 2.24.0.
Sorted inputs are an optional prerequisite for low-memory mode.
outputs: Per-A overlap count, covered-base count, A length and fraction covered; optional depth at each A position and per-feature/overall coverage histograms. Example shell post-processing makes BEDGRAPH-like columns.
dependencies: bedtools coverage; optional shell cut/awk for the documented BEDGRAPH transformations.
The input interval definitions and assembly must match; counting split alignments by span or blocks is a task choice.
evidence: coverage.rst states that coverage is reported on A and computes both depth and fraction of A bases overlapped; it documents -hist, -d, threshold, strand, split and sorted options.
example-usage.rst gives reads.bed over windows10kb.bed and derives counts or fraction-covered values from columns.
limitations: Example alignments and windows are generic names with no accession or provenance in the inspected docs.
Coverage is relative to chosen A intervals and B feature semantics; task author must choose whether reads, fragments or split blocks are intended.

title: Summarize genome-wide feature coverage depth

sources.locator: Overview; Usage and option summary; histogram/BEDGRAPH modes; -split, -strand, -scale, fragment coverage

scientific_use: Calculate per-base or histogram summaries of feature depth across a genome, including uncovered regions, strand-specific depth, scaled depth, or estimated/pair-end fragment coverage. Tutorial frames genome-wide coverage distributions as evidence about WGS coverage uniformity.
tool_role_basis: The source applies the bedtools genomecov command to existing alignments/features and a genome definition; it does not implement a new genome-coverage method.
inputs: BED/GFF/VCF intervals plus a genome file listing chromosome lengths, or position-sorted BAM input.
Optional settings identify blocked/spliced alignments, strand, 5-prime/3-prime positions, scaling factor, or fragment-size assumptions.
outputs: Coverage histogram, per-position depth, or BEDGRAPH intervals with depth; -bga includes zero-depth spans.
Can be chained with interval intersection to extract uncovered portions of target regions.
dependencies: bedtools genomecov; sorted/grouped interval input and genome-size file for text interval input, or position-sorted BAM.
A normalization factor or estimated fragment length requires an externally chosen value; the docs give RPM as a possible scale rationale.
evidence: genomecov.rst defines histogram, per-base and BEDGRAPH modes, requires a genome file for BED-like input, and describes zero coverage, split alignments and fragment modes.
The tutorial demonstrates exons plus genome.txt and describes genome-wide depth histogram; it also shows a chain to intersect uncovered coverage with capture regions.

title: Compare genomic interval sets by Jaccard similarity

sources.locator: Overview; Default behavior; overlap-fraction options
Jaccard comparisons of fetal-heart DNase hypersensitivity samples; 20-sample pairwise matrix, hierarchical clustering/PCA and heatmap example

scientific_use: Summarize similarity between two genomic interval sets as intersection base pairs divided by union base pairs; tutorial compares DNase hypersensitivity intervals from two fetal-heart samples and proposes a pairwise similarity matrix across 20 fetal tissue samples for higher-order comparison.
tool_role_basis: The source demonstrates applying bedtools jaccard to existing interval sets and then using GNU parallel/Python/R for matrix and visualization steps; it is use/composition of tools, not creation of the bedtools statistic.
inputs: Two genomic interval sets in BED/GFF/VCF format, presorted by chromosome and start.
For tutorial matrix workflow, a collection of merged DNase hotspot BED files and labels are assumed; sample identifiers include fHeart-DS16621, fHeart-DS15839 and fSkin_fibro_bicep_R-DS19745.hg19.
outputs: Intersection length, union-minus-intersection length, Jaccard score, and number of intersections.
When composed across pairs, a similarity matrix that tutorial subsequently loads into R for PCA/heatmap exploration.
dependencies: For the tutorial matrix composition: GNU parallel, a linked make-matrix.py script, R, ggplot2, RColorBrewer; gplots for heatmap. These historical dependencies require availability/version review.
evidence: jaccard.rst defines the interval-set statistic and output columns, sorting requirement, and overlap fraction filters; it cites Favorov et al. (2012), DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1002529.
tutorial gives two DNase-sample comparison commands/results and describes a 20-by-20 set of pairwise comparisons followed by R dimensionality-reduction and heatmap examples.
limitations: Tutorial BED files and the make-matrix.py script are not pinned to an accessible data/script revision in the inspected source; filenames alone do not establish dataset access, study design, or reuse terms.

title: Estimate interval-overlap enrichment with Fisher's exact test

sources.locator: Worked 500-base and 60-base examples; Evaluation; Usage and options

scientific_use: Assess whether overlap between two interval sets is unexpectedly high or low under an estimated universe of possible intervals; report contingency counts and left-, right-, and two-tailed p-values. Documentation warns that the universe estimate uses mean interval sizes and genome length and can inflate significance; recommends validating low p-values with simulation.
tool_role_basis: The documented command applies bedtools fisher to existing feature files and a genome-size definition; the source's evaluation compares its result with simulated shuffled data, not a new solver-authored statistical implementation.
inputs: Two BED/GFF/VCF feature files and genome file listing chromosome lengths.
Optional minimum-overlap fraction and strand/split semantics affect overlap counts.
Interpretation requires the heuristic estimate of the number of possible intervals; interval size distributions and genome size are central inputs.
outputs: Counts of query intervals, database intervals, overlaps, estimated possible intervals, a contingency table, p-values for both tails and two-tail, and an overlap ratio.
dependencies: bedtools fisher; sorted inputs are documented as required.
A stated genome length and scientifically defensible interpretation of the heuristic null/universe.
evidence: fisher.rst includes explicit two-feature examples and shows how changing a toy genome from 500 to 60 bases changes the inferred possible interval count and p-values.

The Evaluation section says its plot compares Fisher p-values with simulations using canonical genes on chr1 and randomized 3000 intervals of lengths 20 to 5250 bases, repeated 1000 times; these are documentation claims, not reproduced here.
limitations: Statistical suitability is provisional: the possible-interval count is heuristic and the docs report p-value inflation, advising simulation checks.
Evaluation fixture's gene annotation source/version and randomization implementation are not resolved in this pass.
No Fisher calculation or simulation was run.

Related-tool link to reldist

tool_role_basis: The documented workflow applies the existing bedtools reldist utility to bundled BED annotation/reference files; it does not implement the metric.
